cards.headline: Nearly 700,000 people displaced by fighting in southern Ethiopia

pages.text: Nearly 700,000 people have been displaced by clashes between armed forces in southern Ethiopia, according to the British NGO Islamic Relief. The fighting, which has been occurring for nearly a month, involves members of the Oromo and Ethiopian Somali communities. The conflict began in late October following a dispute over control of the border town of Moyale. Islamic Relief stated the conflict has spread up to 300 kilometers (185 miles) from the town, with fighting occurring in areas across ethnic group settlements. The organization reported that many homes have been destroyed and health care services disrupted, while more than 50,000 people have fled to neighboring Kenya. An estimated 329,000 people were displaced from the Dawa zone in the Somali region, while 359,798 had been registered as displaced in southern Oromia.

Kedir Musema Hameza, the head of Islamic Relief’s Ethiopia program, described the situation as a volatile conflict driven by two ethnic groups competing for land and wealth at the borders of Ethiopia. He characterized the mass displacement as a serious humanitarian incident. While the conflict monitor ACLED reported that several people have been killed since the fighting began, no precise death toll is available. The government of Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, who hails from the Oromia region, has not commented on the violence. Regional borders in Ethiopia, which were set by the 1995 constitution, have been a frequent source of conflict in the nation.

cards.headline: Eight injured after driver repeatedly rams car into Palestinians in Kafr Qasim, Israel

pages.text: Eight people were injured on the evening of November 18, 2026, when a driver struck Palestinian residents at four separate locations in the central Israeli city of Kafr Qasim. Social media footage appears to show the car accelerating toward the victims, who were all Palestinians, at several locations in the city before the driver drove away. The Times of Israel reported that three of those injured were in moderate condition and several victims were women leaving a nearby wedding. Investigators are examining whether the driver struck the people deliberately, according to Haaretz. Avi Levy, a police district commander, stated the incident appeared to be a hit-and-run and that the driver had tested positive for drugs. Levy noted that the Shin Bet security service is participating in the investigation and said the suspect has no criminal record, adding, “As of this moment, nothing is coming up.”

The incident has led Arab lawmakers and activists to accuse Israeli politicians of fueling hostility toward Arab citizens. Yousef Jabareen, the chair of the Joint List, said the event “raises difficult questions about the claim that the driver lost control,” noting he had warned for weeks that incitement against Arab citizens could lead to assaults or assassinations. Said Issa, a community activist in Kafr Qasim, described the incident as an “act of terror.” These accusations follow comments from Benjamin Netanyahu, who has called Arab parties “terror supporters” and stated that partnering with them would jeopardize Israel’s security. Arab parties recently won a record 19 seats in the Knesset, Israel's parliament.

cards.headline: Russian President Putin vows 'far more painful' response to Ukrainian strikes on Crimean Bridge

pages.text: Russian President Vladimir Putin has vowed that Moscow's retaliation for attacks on the Crimean Bridge will be “far more painful” than the strikes carried out by Kyiv. Putin made the statement during a press conference in Shenzhen, China, following a summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump. The comments follow a combined missile-and-drone strike on November 17, 2026, that destroyed the central road section of the 12-mile, double-arched bridge connecting Russia to the occupied Crimean Peninsula, causing part of the structure to collapse into the water and rendering it unusable for road traffic. This event marked the third time the bridge has been hit. On November 18, 2026, the bridge was attacked again, temporarily halting traffic. Sergei Aksyonov, the Moscow-appointed head of Crimea, stated on Telegram that an assessment of the damage is underway.

The bridge, which was unveiled in 2018, is a critical logistical link used by Russia to resupply troops in southern Ukraine and to carry out strikes across the country. While Kyiv has alleged the bridge is used to transport military equipment, Putin claimed during his press conference that the bridge is used exclusively for civilian purposes and not for petroleum products or military transport. Ukraine's defence ministry stated that the strikes amounted to “time gained and lives saved,” arguing that reducing the supplies reaching occupiers protects Ukrainian warriors. Ukraine previously declared the bridge, which crosses the Kerch strait, to be illegal. Since the 2014 annexation of Crimea, Moscow has utilized the peninsula as a military base containing airbases, artillery stockpiles, training grounds, and troop concentrations.

Ukraine stated that the November 17, 2026, strike was carried out using Neptune cruise missiles. Separately, the Dutch-headquartered startup Destinus confirmed that its Ruta cruise missiles were the only foreign-made weapons used in the attack. Following this confirmation, the Russian embassy in the Netherlands posted a statement on X asking if the Netherlands had openly joined the conflict, noting that Moscow had been informed of the company's involvement. The collapse of the bridge's arch represents the most significant damage inflicted on the structure in several years.

cards.headline: Trump, Putin, and Xi issue joint declaration on peace following talks in China

pages.text: Donald Trump, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin issued a joint declaration on peace on November 19, 2026, following a trilateral summit in Shenzhen, China. The three leaders, who met for 90 minutes, vowed to engage in dialogue regarding the reduction of nuclear risks and the reform of the United Nations. The declaration also stated plans to increase supplies of petroleum products. While the leaders addressed the media together from a large conference table, a BBC North America correspondent noted that the joint statement provided minimal substance despite the rhetoric and imagery.

During the summit, President Xi Jinping stated that global powers bear “special responsibilities” in an interconnected world. President Trump remarked that “no peace was ever forged by declining opportunities for engagement,” while President Putin called for constructive co-operation. Before the trilateral meeting, Trump held individual discussions with both Putin and Xi. Trump described Putin as his “friend,” noting they have had a “great relationship for many years,” and told Xi that the United States and China have made “significant strides” in improving economic ties over the past year and a half.

The summit took place as Russian strikes were hitting Kyiv, Ukraine, according to a BBC Eastern Europe correspondent reporting from the Ukrainian capital. The correspondent noted that these strikes occurred as Putin spoke of peace in China.

cards.headline: South Korean Supreme Court overturns 15-year prison sentence for former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo

pages.text: The South Korean Supreme Court has overturned a 15-year prison sentence for former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo, ruling that prosecutors had not sufficiently proven the case against him. Han had been convicted for his role in the 2024 imposition of martial law by former President Yoon Suk Yeol. The case will now return to the Seoul High Court, which had originally sentenced Han to 15 years in prison in May. On December 3, 2024, Yoon Suk Yeol abruptly declared martial law, an action he stated was necessary to remove what he called 'pro-North Korean forces.' The declaration led to massive protests and a confrontation in parliament after Yoon sent troops and police into the assembly. Lawmakers eventually entered the assembly chamber and voted unanimously to reject the decree, forcing the cabinet to rescind it. Yoon was subsequently impeached and sentenced to life in prison after being found guilty of leading an insurrection. Han's conviction was based on allegations that he helped plan the insurrection by suggesting Yoon hold a Cabinet meeting to make the martial law declaration appear legitimate. He also allegedly attempted to collect signatures from Cabinet members on a related document and reviewed orders to cut off power and water to media outlets critical of Yoon.

While the Supreme Court overturned the sentence for Han, it upheld a four-year prison term for Kim Keon Hee, the wife of former President Yoon Suk Yeol. Kim was convicted on corruption charges, which included bribery and the manipulation of stock prices.

cards.headline: Violent protests and killings erupt in Bangladesh ahead of Sheikh Hasina’s planned return

pages.text: Violent protests, bomb blasts, and arson attacks have broken out across parts of Bangladesh as supporters of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina demonstrate against the government's rejection of her request for a new passport and identity card. The Awami League, Hasina's political party, called for a week-long program of rallies and protests to mobilize support for her planned return in December, culminating in a nationwide lockdown attempt. Hasina has lived in exile in India since fleeing Dhaka following protests that demanded her resignation in August 2024. The attempted shutdown was reported as mostly successful in southern districts where the Awami League maintains strong support.

The unrest has resulted in several deaths and significant property damage. On November 17, 2026, police reported that an activist of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) was allegedly killed by unidentified people during a protest near Gopalganj, Hasina's home district. On the night of November 18, 2026, police stated that two members of the ruling BNP had been killed. During that same night, the ancestral home of former interim leader Muhammad Yunus in Chattogram was set on fire; police noted it is likely flammable substances were thrown into an unused ground-floor room, though Yunus' paternal family members living on the upper floors were safe. Other reported violence includes a crude bomb exploding outside the Dhaka residence of cultural affairs minister Nitai Roy Chowdhury, the vandalism and burning of the houses of two BNP lawmakers in Gopalganj, and the setting of shops belonging to BNP supporters on fire.

The scale of the instability includes dozens of crude bomb blasts and incidents of vehicles being set on fire in at least 28 districts over a 10-day period, according to police and media reports. Specific incidents included at least six buses and pickup vans being set on fire along with a section of railway line, and a bus and truck being set on fire on the Dhaka-Chattogram highway. To deter further violence, 97 platoons of the Bangladesh Border Guard, a paramilitary force, fanned out across seven districts, including Gopalganj and Faridpur. Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has accused Awami League leaders of conspiring against the country and suggested they are acting to satisfy masters in the country across the border, referring to India, without naming the nation explicitly.

cards.headline: Surgeon calls for criminal investigation into Scottish hospital after at least 19 deaths

pages.text: Dr. Mohammed Habib, a consultant at Aberdeen Royal Infirmary in Scotland, has called for a police investigation into corporate homicide following reports that at least 19 patients died from avoidable complications due to surgery. Habib, who has reported concerns regarding liver and pancreatic surgery at the hospital from 2021 onwards, alleged that senior officials at NHS Grampian—the health board responsible for the hospital—failed to take sufficient or timely action. Habib stated he believes dozens of patients may have died unnecessarily at the facility. An internal report, published by Habib’s solicitor Aamer Anwar, confirmed allegations that 19 patients died due to “serious adverse events” caused by surgery between 2015 and 2021.

Scotland’s first minister, John Swinney, described Habib’s disclosures as being “of the gravest concern” and noted that the NHS has legal duties to provide patients with the best possible care and to investigate safety failure allegations quickly. However, Swinney rebuffed demands from Scottish Labour leader Michael Marra for a criminal investigation into what Marra described as “systemic failures” at NHS Grampian. Marra stated that the families of the 19 deceased individuals deserve justice and answers. Swinney denied that the government had ignored Habib’s complaints, stating that a recent decision to demand urgent reforms and changes of leadership at the board should result in necessary improvements.

cards.headline: International Court of Justice finds Myanmar guilty of genocide

pages.text: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) has issued a verdict finding Myanmar guilty of committing genocide, making it the first country in history to receive such a ruling. In a nine-to-six majority decision, judges in The Hague established a detailed roadmap for applying the 1948 Genocide Convention to real-world situations, specifically regarding how to assess a government's intent when accused of committing genocide against a population group. This ruling provides a benchmark for the International Criminal Court (ICC), a sister tribunal that handles genocide charges against individual perpetrators.

Legal experts and human rights organizations have described the decision as a way to give the Genocide Convention practical meaning. Philippe Sands, a human rights lawyer on the Gambian legal team, stated the judgment “brings the genocide convention alive” and prevents the convention from becoming a “dead letter.” Agnès Callamard, secretary general of Amnesty International, called the ruling “a rare moment of justice for survivors, victims and their families.” Dr. Iva Vukušić, an assistant professor in international history at Utrecht University and a war crimes expert, noted the ruling clarifies international law and serves as an assertion of humanitarian law. The verdict is also considered relevant to Israel, which is the only other country currently before the ICJ accused of genocide, and to Germany, which Nicaragua has brought before the court on accusations of facilitating and failing to prevent genocide in Gaza.

cards.headline: Anthropic raises $81bn in record-breaking stock market debut

pages.text: Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI chatbot, has raised a record $81bn (£62bn) in a stock market debut that will make it one of the most valuable companies in the world. The five-year-old firm, which was established in 2021, is the first purely AI-focused company to publicly sell its shares. High investor appetite for the loss-making business resulted in more stock being sold than originally planned, with shares priced at $83, exceeding the proposed $70-$78 range. Shares are scheduled to begin trading in New York, valuing the company at approximately $1.5 trillion on a diluted basis, which is a valuation that accounts for factors such as employee stock options. On a basic share count, Anthropic is worth about $1.1tn, a figure more valuable than Walmart and Samsung but less than Tesla and Meta.

The flotation serves as a crucial test for the fast-growing artificial intelligence sector. While global spending on AI approaches $850 billion in 2026, questions are being raised regarding whether and when massive investments in AI infrastructure and tools will pay off. During the Nasdaq listing, co-founders Dario and Daniela Amodei rang the opening bell to celebrate the start of trading. The listing overtook the June offering by SpaceX. The seven founders of Anthropic will become multi-billionaires immediately following the debut.

Outside the Nasdaq, protesters demonstrated against the flotation and the concentration of tech-sector wealth, an event that saw three people detained by police. Demonstrators warned that ordinary investors could pay the price if the AI surge ends in a financial bust. Protester Jose Gonzalez questioned who would bear the brunt of a market reversal, arguing that wealthy investors have protections unavailable to the public. While enthusiasts hail a technological revolution, economists and watchdogs have warned of a looming financial bubble, growing inequality, swelling debt, and fears that automation could wipe out jobs and funnel wealth to a few tech titans.

cards.headline: Alberta legislation would require oil and gas companies to fund cleanup for every new well

pages.text: The Alberta government has introduced legislation that would require oil and gas companies to set aside funds for the future cleanup of every new well drilled. If passed, the bill would create the Resource Asset Closure Assurance and Stewardship Fund to ensure money is available for decommissioning sites, preventing taxpayers from being responsible for cleanup costs. Energy and Minerals Minister Brian Jean stated at a news conference that the combination of payments and accrued compound interest should provide enough money to fund the eventual cleanup of a typical well. The new rules are expected to apply to wells drilled after April 1, 2027.

Under the proposed rules, funds would follow each well through its entire life cycle, even if the ownership of the well changes hands. Companies would be required to make an initial payment of up to $50,000, followed by equal annual payments for up to 10 years. This measure addresses the long-running issue in Alberta of managing a backlog of old oil and gas wells that have no one legally responsible for them due to factors such as bankruptcy. Farmers have expressed concerns regarding potential contamination from inactive wells on their land.

The proposed fund would exist alongside the current system for managing orphan wells. Cleanup of sites with no responsible owner is currently managed through the Orphan Well Association, a non-profit funded by an industry fee recommended annually by the Alberta Energy Regulator. That fee would continue to exist. The Orphan Well Levy for the 2026-27 fiscal year is $154.56 million, an increase from $144.45 million the previous year, while the Orphan Well Association has estimated total cleanup costs for its inventory at $1.66 billion.

cards.headline: Dozens missing after migrant boat capsizes off Senegal's coast

pages.text: Senegalese authorities are conducting search operations for dozens of missing people after a boat carrying migrants and refugees capsized in the Atlantic Ocean. The vessel, described as a dilapidated pirogue, washed ashore near the village of Yenne, south of Dakar, after reportedly striking a rocky area. While reports on the number of fatalities vary, four bodies have been reported recovered so far; Yenne Mayor Massamba Mbengue and local firefighters stated one body was recovered, while two other local sources reported two bodies. A survivor questioned by the gendarmerie told police there were approximately 100 people on the boat, including five women. However, a local official told Reuters the vessel was carrying 50 people. An official stated the boat hit a rock while migrants were transferring from small fishing boats to a larger vessel.

The incident occurred around 02:00 GMT, according to Oumar Sow, a representative of the village chief, who said cries from the pirogue were audible from the beach. Police and gendarmerie recovered personal belongings from the wreckage, including identity documents, several mobile phones, water sachets, and a school enrolment document belonging to a high school student from Kabrousse. An official noted that Yenne has become a migration embarkation point where smugglers recruit boat pilots. This tragedy follows a shipwreck off the coast of the north-western town of Thieppe approximately 10 days earlier that killed at least 39 or 43 people, marking one of Senegal's deadliest migration disasters. At a cabinet meeting on November 18, 2026, President Diomaye Faye expressed concern regarding a renewed increase in irregular departures by migrants attempting to reach Europe.

The human rights group Action for Human Rights and Friendship (ADHA) in Senegal has called for a parliamentary inquiry into the tragedy, denouncing a lack of lasting results in reducing migrant deaths at sea. Many West Africans attempt to reach Spain's Canary Islands via the Atlantic route, often using overloaded and unseaworthy boats. On November 10, Spain declared a migration emergency in the Canary Islands following the arrival of more than 9,000 people since the start of November. Spain’s Maritime Rescue Service reported rescuing 1,488 migrants aboard 14 dinghies, most of whom arrived on El Hierro from West Africa on November 14, breaking a previous record of 1,461 people rescued in November 2020.

cards.headline: Aid groups grade Trump Gaza peace plan at four out of 26 points

pages.text: A coalition of five international aid organizations has issued a humanitarian scorecard grading the Trump administration’s 20-point Comprehensive Plan to end the Gaza Conflict at just four out of 26 possible points. The assessment comes one year after the United Nations Security Council endorsed the plan. The coalition—comprising the Danish Refugee Council, Norwegian Refugee Council, Oxfam, Refugees International, and Save the Children—reported that the plan scored zero on humanitarian access and earned one point for civilian protection. The groups released the scorecard as Israeli forces launched a new ground offensive in central Gaza, advancing with tanks west of a military “Yellow Line” and issuing new forced evacuation orders. Aid groups state these actions violate the peace plan, which explicitly prohibits territorial occupation in Gaza and requires Israeli forces to withdraw.

The expansion of Israeli military control has confined approximately 2.1 million Palestinians to a shrinking area. According to OCHA, Israeli control of Gaza territory grew from 58 percent at the start of the ceasefire 13 months ago to 65 percent on November 19, 2026. A UN official told the UN Security Council in June that Israel itself has stated it controls 70 percent of the territory. Because Palestinians are not permitted to cross the military line, OCHA reports they are now squeezed into 128 square km (49 square miles), a density of 16,000 people per square km. However, a map analysis by the US news group NPR suggests the confinement area may be as small as 109 square km (42 square miles), resulting in a population density of nearly 19,300 people per square km. Ramy Abdu, founder and chairman of the Euro-Mediterranean Human Rights Monitor, warned that Israel is carrying out unlawful acquisition of territory by force.

Since the ceasefire was declared in October, agencies report at least 1,650 Palestinians have been killed and 5,975 wounded. Shaun Hughes, the World Food Programme (WFP) country director for Palestine, told journalists that Israeli military control across nearly 70 percent of Gaza leaves people with almost no space to grow food and makes fishing in the sea prohibited and life-threatening. Hughes noted that unemployment is over 80 percent, leaving people with little or no alternate means of survival without humanitarian assistance.

cards.headline: United States and Venezuela sign military cooperation agreement

pages.text: The United States and Venezuela re-established military ties on November 18, 2026, less than a year after U.S. forces seized former Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro during a raid in Caracas. U.S. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth signed a military co-operation agreement with Venezuela's interim government, led by acting president Delcy Rodríguez, during a visit to the capital that had not been publicly announced in advance. Hegseth, who met Rodríguez at the presidential palace, described Venezuela as having transitioned from the country's most aggressive regional threat to a compliant security partner in less than 12 months.

While specific details of the agreement have not been fully released, Rodríguez stated the deal would allow for the resumption of technical and military cooperation, including improving the training and equipment of the Venezuelan armed forces to confront common threats. Hegseth noted the partnership would support cooperation regarding economic issues and the fight against criminal networks and drug trafficking. This development follows the January 3 seizure of Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, by U.S. Delta Force operatives. Both Maduro and Flores are currently in custody in New York facing charges of drug-trafficking and conspiracy to commit torture, which they deny.

The agreement ends a period of severed military ties that began in 2005 when then-president Hugo Chávez terminated cooperation. Chávez had alleged that U.S. military personnel training Venezuelan counterparts made disparaging remarks about his government and accused a U.S. military office at the Fuerte Tiuna complex of being a CIA organ conspiring against the state. Relations deteriorated further under Maduro, culminating in the U.S. doubling the reward for information leading to his capture to $50 million. Hegseth, addressing a speech at the U.S. embassy in Caracas, called himself the first U.S. Secretary of War this century to set foot in Venezuela.

cards.headline: Ontario elementary teachers and education workers vote 97% in favour of strike action

pages.text: Ontario English public elementary teachers and education workers have voted overwhelmingly in favour of strike action, according to the Elementary Teachers' Federation of Ontario (ETFO). The union reported that 97 per cent of teachers and occasional teachers, as well as 97 per cent of education workers, voted to provide the union with strike mandates. A strike mandate is a vote that authorizes a union to take strike action but does not mean a strike will occur, as additional legal steps are required before a strike can take place. The ETFO represents approximately 84,000 members, including 80,000 public elementary teachers and occasional teachers, and about 4,000 education workers such as designated early childhood educators, education support staff, and professional support staff.

ETFO President David Mastin said the strike mandates reflect growing challenges in schools and worksites across Ontario and serve as a message to the Ontario government and the Council of Ontario Directors of Education. Mastin stated that members are frustrated by years of chronic underfunding and deteriorating learning and working conditions. The union's bargaining priorities include smaller class sizes, stronger health and safety protections, job security, fair compensation, and measures to address classroom complexity and composition. Negotiations are expected to resume at the end of November for both the teachers' and education workers' central tables. Current education contracts expired at the end of August, but negotiations are currently stalled while the Ontario Labour Relations Board decides which issues should be bargained centrally and which should be left to local unions and school boards.

Other provincial teaching associations have also issued strike mandates. Teachers represented by the Ontario Secondary School Teachers’ Federation voted 96 per cent in favour of a strike mandate, while the union representing 45,000 teachers in Ontario’s English Catholic schools voted 98 per cent in favour.

cards.headline: US-led consortium wins tender for Kenya's $60bn Mrima Hill mineral project

pages.text: Frontier Minerals, a US-led consortium, has won the tender to develop the Mrima Hill mining project in Kwale County, Kenya. The consortium beat seven other bidders, including companies from China and Australia. The site is estimated to hold deposits of critical minerals worth more than $60bn, including niobium, which is used in aerospace, defence technology, and electric vehicles. This development comes as Washington seeks to strengthen US supply chains and compete with China, which currently dominates the processing of several key minerals and the mining and processing of critical minerals across Africa. To proceed, the consortium must still obtain a prospecting licence and meet necessary regulatory requirements.

The Frontier Minerals consortium is composed of three US companies: Bunker Hill Mining Corp, American Resources Corporation, and ReElement Technologies Corporation. The group combines expertise in advanced refining technologies, critical materials supply chains, and mineral resource development. A central part of the proposal is to develop mineral processing and refining capacity within Kenya. Brad Barnett of Frontier Minerals stated the company intends to help the country capture more value from its resources by processing and refining minerals in-country. Barnett also said the company intends to create opportunities for Kenyan businesses, workers, and the wider economy through targeted investment and capacity-building while prioritizing environmental management.

The Mrima Hill site covers approximately 390 acres of forest near the Kenyan Indian Ocean coastline. The prospect of mining has raised concerns among local residents regarding potential damage to the forest and threats to their ancestral heritage. Additionally, there are questions regarding whether communities living near the site will benefit from the investment. The tender decision has also faced objections from competitors. Reuters reports that two rival companies intend to challenge the selection, including Australia's RareX, which alleges that Frontier Minerals missed an earlier submission deadline. The Kenyan government has maintained that the process was transparent and open.

cards.headline: Cairo court suspends trial of Mada Masr editor Lina Attalah

pages.text: A court in Cairo, Egypt, has suspended proceedings in the trial of Lina Attalah, the chief editor of the independent news outlet Mada Masr, following a defense request for the recusal of the judge. A separate court is scheduled to rule on the request for Judge Mohamed Mubarak to step down from the case on November 26. Attalah faces up to a year in prison on charges of publishing false news and operating a website without a license. Mada Masr stated on X that proceedings are suspended until that ruling is issued. This trial is a retrial after Attalah learned during an October trial that she had received a one-year prison sentence in absentia in 2024 without her knowledge.

The defense team, consisting of eight lawyers, argued that Judge Mohamed Mubarak had already formed a conviction against Attalah. They cited a previous ruling against her in a separate case that they described as a rush trial. In an interview with AFP, Attalah said the judge had insisted the case was a simple matter that required no time. During a previous session, Mubarak appointed his own lawyer for Attalah, wrote the defense statement on her behalf, fined her three million Egyptian pounds (approximately $56,000), and ordered the closure of Mada Masr. Mada Masr has stated it applied for a license several times, but its applications have gone largely unanswered.

The prosecution of Attalah has drawn criticism from rights groups and the United Nations. The UN has criticized what it described as widening attacks on press freedom in Egypt, stating that Attalah's prosecution raises questions regarding fair-trial guarantees and due process. Mada Masr has operated for more than a decade despite a crackdown on press freedom in Egypt, and Cairo has faced long-standing criticism regarding its rights record.

cards.headline: US Defence Secretary announces military partnership with Venezuela's interim government

pages.text: United States Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth has announced a new agreement with Venezuela’s interim government to facilitate military cooperation between the two countries. During a surprise visit to Caracas that was not previously announced by the Pentagon, Hegseth stated the deal will include intelligence sharing and joint training for the militaries of both nations. Hegseth described the agreement as a reestablishment of a defence partnership intended to stabilise Venezuela and eliminate narco-terrorists. He was hosted by interim President Delcy Rodriguez, the former vice president who has led the government since her swearing-in on January 5.

The agreement follows a period of heavy US influence over Rodriguez and her government. On January 3, the Trump administration conducted a military attack that resulted in the abduction of former President Nicolas Maduro. President Donald Trump justified the operation as a law enforcement effort to ensure Maduro stands trial on American soil regarding weapons- and drug-related crimes. Following that operation, Trump told The Atlantic magazine that he planned to “run” Venezuela and suggested Rodriguez could “pay a very big price, probably bigger than Maduro” if she does not comply with US demands.

cards.headline: Ghana Armed Forces reclaim 50 hectares of land destroyed by illegal mining in Tano-Nimiri Forest Reserve

pages.text: The 14 Engineer Brigade of the Ghana Armed Forces has reclaimed 50 hectares of land devastated by illegal mining at the Tano-Nimiri Forest Reserve in Samreboi, located in the Western Region of Ghana. The reclamation project aims to restore the degraded forest reserve, improve access to affected areas, and prevent further environmental destruction. On Wednesday, November 18, 2026, the first phase of the project was formally handed over to the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod). This phase involved extensive engineering works to rehabilitate abandoned mining pits and damaged watercourses.

To restore the area, the 14 Engineer Brigade performed several engineering tasks, including the excavation and backfilling of abandoned mine pits, reshaping and grading of disturbed land, drainage improvements, and the spreading of topsoil. The Brigade also reopened blocked watercourses to restore the natural flow of water through the site. Additionally, the project included the construction of 13.6 kilometres of access roads to facilitate movement through the difficult terrain. To assist in long-term protection, a Forward Operating Base (FOB) was constructed to accommodate 10 personnel. This facility, intended for Forestry Commission officers responsible for protecting the reclaimed land, is equipped with a borehole, solar power system, washrooms, and a kitchen.

Brigadier General Richard Kinney, the Commander of the 14 Engineer Brigade, led the handover ceremony. He described the completed project as a testament to the professionalism and discipline of the Ghana Armed Forces engineering team. While noting the completion of the first phase, Brig Gen Kinney stated that the destruction of forest reserves through illegal mining remains a serious threat to national development and the environment. He cautioned that protecting the reclaimed land is a major challenge and called for a sustained, visible presence by the Forestry Commission to prevent illegal miners from returning to the area.

cards.headline: Deaf Nigerians fight to preserve indigenous sign languages

pages.text: Deaf communities in Nigeria are working to preserve indigenous sign languages that existed before the introduction of formal sign language education in the country. These native systems of communication are viewed by community members as essential components of their cultural identity. In Abuja, 37-year-old Umaru Zayyanu uses Hausa sign language, which has become a common way for deaf people to communicate across northern Nigeria. Zayyanu states that these languages are part of his culture and identity, noting that deaf communities possessed their own languages prior to formal schooling. Sanni Lawal, a deaf laundry worker, expressed an ambition to see these indigenous sign languages gain wider recognition and spread beyond their local communities.

Researchers and activists warn that indigenous sign languages face the risk of disappearing due to limited funding, poor documentation, and the growing dominance of formal sign languages. Sign language researcher Taiwo Ajayi says that documenting and developing these languages is essential, particularly for deaf individuals who have never had access to formal education. Activists are calling for increased investment and greater recognition to prevent the loss of Nigeria's linguistic diversity.

cards.headline: Water crisis deepens in Taiz, Yemen, amid Houthi siege

pages.text: Residents in Taiz, Yemen, face a deepening water crisis as fuel shortages and loss of access to wells force many to rely on unsafe water. The situation has intensified following a Houthi siege on the city that began in October, after Houthi forces made advances against government troops in the countryside surrounding Taiz. Taiz is Yemen's third-largest city and has long experienced severe water shortages. Wafiq al-Aghbari, director-general of the Taiz governorate’s Local Water and Sanitation Corporation, stated the crisis intensified in 2015 during the first Houthi siege and has worsened annually since. UNICEF reports that water production in Taiz has nearly halved, while more than 800,000 people are reported to be cut off from humanitarian assistance.

The siege has impacted the cost and availability of clean water. Qaid al-Sharaabi, a resident, told Al Jazeera he waited three days for a clean water tanker and noted that he has had to pay twice the price for a tanker twice since the siege began a month-and-a-half ago. Al-Sharaabi expressed concern that residents may resort to using unsafe water if conditions continue. Hospital administrators have warned of a potential public health disaster, and government officials have expressed uncertainty regarding how much longer they will have the funds to maintain even limited services. The city remains a site of conflict as government soldiers defend it during the latest round of fighting in the war that began in 2014.

cards.headline: Scientists create first whole-body single-cell atlas of an adult vertebrate

pages.text: Researchers from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), the Whitehead Institute for Biomedical Research, and Charité–Universitätsmedizin Berlin have created the first comprehensive map of cell types and gene activity across an entire adult vertebrate. To achieve this, the team profiled more than 600,000 cells from the tiny, transparent fish species *Danionella cerebrum* to build a single-cell transcriptome atlas. This atlas serves as a molecular reference that identifies cell types throughout the fish, the patterns of gene activity that distinguish them, and their locations. A cell's transcriptome is the complete set of RNA molecules it has produced from its DNA at a specific time, which acts as a snapshot of which genes the cell is currently using.

The study, published in *Science* on Oct. 29, utilized *Danionella cerebrum* because its small size makes whole-animal single-cell profiling technically feasible. While cell atlases have become more detailed, profiling the cellular diversity of larger animals is difficult because it is expensive and technically demanding. Because the fish is transparent, its brain is visible through the top of its head. Kutay Deniz Atabay, a postdoc in the lab of MIT biology professor and Whitehead Institute member Peter Reddien, led the work. Atabay noted that a spatially resolved atlas allows researchers to see not only which cell types exist but also the neighbors of those cell types, providing access to biological complexity ranging from the molecular to the systems level.

This whole-body map provides a baseline for researchers to study how changes such as aging, injury, or drugs affect cells across an entire animal. The perspective offered by the atlas may help reveal how cells in different tissues coordinate their responses and how changes in one part of the body influence other areas. The species *Danionella cerebrum* has drawn increasing interest for its unique biology since it was formally described in 2021.

cards.headline: Toys 'R' Us and Parties 'R' Us departments to move into 300 Staples Canada stores

pages.text: Toys 'R' Us Canada and Parties 'R' Us are moving into portions of 300 Staples Canada stores. The partnership aims to bring back the toy retailer, which recently emerged from creditor protection and is now connected to the U.S. firm that owns Party City, Chia Pets, and the Graceland Elvis Presley attraction. For Staples Canada, the move is part of an effort to evolve its brand and convince shoppers the retailer offers more than office supplies, school supplies, or printing services. A Staples Canada location in Richmond Hill, Ontario, north of Toronto, is the first to undergo the transformation. Mike Rinaldi, Staples Canada's chief merchandise officer, stated that the new products are part of an evolving Staples brand.

cards.headline: One in four women globally unable to refuse sex within marriage, UN report finds

pages.text: A report by the UN Population Fund (UNFPA) found that one in four women around the world lack the power of consent if a husband or partner demands sex. In West and Central Africa, 45% of women are unable to say no within their own marriage. In East and Southern Africa and in Arab states, 33% of women face the same situation, while one in 10 women in Latin America and the Caribbean are unable to refuse sex.

An analysis of eight countries with comparable data—Angola, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kazakhstan, Malawi, Mali, Nigeria, Tajikistan, and Zambia—showed that girls and younger women aged 15 to 19 had even less power to refuse sex than women aged 45 to 49. These findings align with research indicating that adolescent girls experience high rates of intimate partner violence.

Jean-Paul Murunga, a lawyer with the human rights organization Equality Now, described the figures as “really sad,” noting that sexual intercourse without free and voluntary consent constitutes sexual violence, including within marriage. Murunga stated that marriage does not create perpetual or implied consent and that a woman retains the right to decide whether, when, and how she engages in sexual activity. He suggested that changing rape laws across the African continent is a necessary first step. He also noted that while the African Union adopted the Maputo protocol in 2003 to set binding legal standards for equality and protect women from violence, work remains to ensure women and girls benefit from those commitments.

cards.headline: New designer opioid found in Toronto fentanyl supply

pages.text: Toronto’s Drug Checking Service has identified a new designer opioid within fentanyl samples, marking the sixth new substance discovered in the city's illicit supply. The substance, which was first detected in four fentanyl samples in October, belongs to the orphine class of opioids—a group of potent designer drugs that global monitors have been increasingly tracking. Because the substance is so new, it does not yet have a generic name. It has also been detected in Vancouver. Scientists have identified the substance as either N'-Phenethyl-5-chloro nor-orphine or N'-Phenethyl-6-chloro nor-orphine, but the two are so chemically similar that the drug checking service cannot currently differentiate between them.

The discovery has raised concerns regarding the evolving and unregulated nature of the street drug supply in Canada. Karen McDonald, executive director of the drug checking service operating out of St. Michael’s Hospital, stated that little is known about the new drug's strength or effects due to a lack of available research. This follows a previous finding by the service of cychlorphine, an orphine-class opioid believed to be approximately 10 times stronger than fentanyl. Cristiana Stefan, a lab director and clinical biochemist at the Centre for Addiction and Mental Health, expressed concern regarding how this new orphine may interact with other drugs.

cards.headline: Astronomers witness a dying star engulfing a neighbor in the Andromeda galaxy

pages.text: Astronomers have observed a stellar engulfment in real time, witnessing a dying star consume mass and energy from a smaller companion star. Located approximately 2.5 million light-years from Earth in the Andromeda galaxy, the collision involves an asymptotic giant branch (AGB) star—a very bright, relatively cool star that has burned nearly all of its nuclear fuel. This discovery, described in a paper in Nature, confirms theoretical ideas about how such stellar collisions occur. The interaction may leave behind a single, rejuvenated remnant star.

The observation began when researchers noticed a star that appeared to be brightening over time. Upon reviewing historical data, the team realized this brightening had been occurring since 2018. The discovery was made by Viraj Karambelkar, a NASA Hubble Fellow at Columbia University, and colleagues while observing the Andromeda galaxy in 2023. They utilized the Wide-Field Infrared Transient Explorer (WINTER) telescope at the Palomar Observatory and NASA’s Near-Earth Object Wide-Field Infrared Survey Explorer (NEOWISE) space telescope to identify the phenomenon.

cards.headline: First Nations-led health unit takes over tuberculosis services in some Manitoba communities

pages.text: Keewatinohk Inniniw Minoayawin Inc., a federally funded First Nations-led public health organization, is taking over some tuberculosis treatment and diagnosis services in First Nations communities previously provided by the Winnipeg Regional Health Authority. Keewatinohk CEO Michelle Monkman said the transition aims to provide more hands-on care and give First Nations more control over healthcare for members in communities disproportionately affected by the disease. Monkman noted that services were previously being delivered more in a virtual capacity, with Winnipeg nurses managing cases without providing hands-on care or support. She added that First Nations communities are often understaffed and busy dealing with emergencies, making it difficult to prioritize tuberculosis.

Manitoba had the highest rate of tuberculosis cases among Canada's provinces in 2025, with 225 cases reported according to federal data. The province's incidence rate of 14.9 per 100,000 people more than doubled the national average. Data shows Manitoba's tuberculosis rates have consistently led most of the country in the decade leading up to 2026. In 2025, 80.6 per cent of people who had tuberculosis were born outside Canada, while Indigenous people represented 11.4 per cent of cases. Monkman stated that most high-incidence communities in Manitoba are located in the north.

cards.headline: Indigenous groups in Sarawak, Malaysia, place memorial stone following victory over oil palm concession

pages.text: Indigenous communities in Malaysian Borneo gathered on Nov. 4 to place the Ba Besanan Memorial Stone in the forest. The Berawan, Penan, and Tering peoples used the gathering to commemorate a three-year battle against an oil palm plantation that threatened their native customary land rights and endangered a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Willie Kajan, an Indigenous Tering member representing the Berawan and Tering in Mulu, stated the stone serves as both a celebration and a warning to current and future generations about outside interests seeking to profit from their native customary land. Kajan noted that the communities cannot overstate the victory but cautioned, “We don’t know their next tactic.”

The conflict began in 2018 when residents detected logging by employees of Radiant Lagoon Sdn. Bhd., a Malaysian firm. The company held rights to a 4,400-hectare (nearly 11,000-acre) oil palm concession that overlapped with Gunung Mulu National Park. The nearly 53,000-hectare (131,000-acre) park has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2000 due to the diversity of species in its forests, karst mountains, and caves. The Berawan, Penan, and Tering peoples live within and around the park and rely on the land for cultural preservation and their livelihoods.

In response to the land clearing, the communities filed a petition, organized blockades, and issued a lawsuit alleging the company violated their rights to native customary land. Kajan said the government made no effort to inform the broader community of the plantation, adding that only a few elected leaders were informed before clearing began. In 2022, the Sarawak government revoked Radiant Lagoon’s concession rights, though it did not disclose its reasoning for the decision.

cards.headline: Physicists use gravity to transmit message through brick wall

pages.text: Physicists at the University of Queensland in Australia have successfully used gravity to transmit a message through a brick wall in a proof-of-concept experiment. By measuring changes in a gravitational field, researchers sent the word “gravity” in binary code through approximately 70cm of solid material using a 1.8-tonne elevator counterweight to represent bits of data. While the method is currently extremely slow, scientists describe it as a “practically unblockable wireless communication scheme” because, unlike electromagnetic signals used for Wi-Fi or phone reception, gravitational signals cannot be screened out by placing ordinary material in their path. The research was published in the journal Science Advances.

The experiment involved moving a 1.8-tonne elevator counterweight up and down between two floors to represent 0 and 1 in binary code. To detect these changes, researchers placed a gravimeter—a sensitive device used to measure the strength of a gravitational field—on the floor of a men's bathroom adjacent to the lift. At a transmission rate of one bit per minute, it took nearly an hour to send the single word “gravity” (1000111 1110010 1100001 1110110 1101001 1110100 1111001). Despite the successful transmission, study co-author Prof Matthew Davis noted that it is currently difficult to imagine how the technology could be practically useful, adding that NASA’s Voyager 1 spacecraft could communicate with Earth at a faster data rate than this concept. Co-author Dr Charles Woffinden of the University of Queensland's school of mathematics and physics noted the appeal of a signal that cannot be blocked by tunnels or solid walls.

cards.headline: Manitoba judge stays impaired driving charges after RCMP officer withheld information about relationship with witness

pages.text: A Manitoba provincial court judge stayed impaired driving charges against a woman after determining an investigating RCMP officer appeared to have deliberately withheld information regarding a romantic relationship with a key witness. Provincial court Judge Victoria Cornick ruled in an October decision that the officer's actions violated the woman's Charter rights, leading to a stay of proceedings. The woman had previously entered a guilty plea, which she later withdrew following the discovery of the officer's relationship with a witness. According to Judge Cornick, the connection between the officer and the witness was discovered by chance when a Crown prosecutor encountered the couple at a Canadian Tire.

The case originated from an investigation by the RCMP into a serious car crash that occurred outside of Flin Flon on March 4, 2023. During the investigation, lead investigator Constable Christopher Chelmecki learned in an interview that the woman might have been consuming alcohol. While officers sought evidence of alcohol consumption, hospital personnel informed them that a production order—a court order used to compel the production of documents or evidence—would be required to access her medical records. Approximately one month after the crash, Corporal Jordan Tost informed Chelmecki that two nurses at the Flin Flon hospital were potential witnesses and suggested that Chelmecki interview them.

Matt Gould, the lawyer for the woman, described the decision to stay the charges as a rare occurrence reserved for cases that represent a clear problem. Gould stated that in almost 20 years of practice, he had not witnessed such behavior from the police, noting that the situation highlights a vulnerability in the legal system's reliance on the assumption that police act with integrity, honesty, and forthrightness without omitting critical facts. Gould characterized the ease with which the officer's omissions could have gone unnoticed as 'chilling.'

cards.headline: Low-intensity focused ultrasound may temporarily ease delusions in adults with chronic psychosis

pages.text: A small pilot trial suggests that directing gentle, noninvasive sound waves deep into the brain may temporarily reduce the severity of delusions in adults living with chronic psychosis. In a randomized comparison against a fake stimulation session, 10 outpatients who received 10 minutes of low-intensity focused ultrasound directed at a deep brain hub showed a moderate drop in delusion severity without experiencing serious side effects, according to preliminary findings published in npj Acoustics. Delusions are fixed beliefs that persist even when contradicted by everyday evidence, and while standard antipsychotic medications quiet these symptoms for many, a substantial number of patients continue to experience them despite ongoing drug treatment.

The research targets abnormal signaling in neural pathways that connect the cerebral cortex—the brain's outer layer—with central relay structures including the striatum, the thalamus, and the globus pallidus. Specifically, the study focused on the globus pallidus interna, a cluster of nerve cells located near the middle of the brain beneath the cortex. This area acts as a primary output gate that sends dopamine-influenced signals to the thalamus, helping the brain filter incoming information to judge which everyday events deserve attention. A 2023 brain-imaging study by the same research group found that unmedicated patients experiencing a first episode of schizophrenia showed unusually heightened communication between the right anterior globus pallidus interna and the dorsal anterior cingulate gyrus, a frontal brain region involved in weighing attention. Stronger signaling along that link tracked with worse psychotic symptoms, identifying the right globus pallidus interna as a candidate for brain stimulation.

cards.headline: Manitoba judge orders government to disclose why Tesla was excluded from electric vehicle rebate program

pages.text: A Manitoba judge has ordered the NDP government of Wab Kinew to disclose who decided to exclude Tesla Motors Canada from the province's electric vehicle (EV) rebate program and the reasoning behind that decision. In an order issued Nov. 13, Court of King's Bench Justice Elissa Neville described the move as an “exceptional and unusual” remedy. The order requires the government to produce a complete record of the decision-making process that disqualified anyone purchasing Tesla vehicles after March 19, 2025, from receiving Manitoba's EV rebates within 10 days. This legal action follows a request made by Tesla in May to overturn the exclusion.

Tesla has argued for six months that the decision to exclude its vehicles was unreasonable, unfair, and untransparent. The company contends it remains unclear who made the decision to disqualify Tesla vehicles or whether that individual had the legal authority to do so. The Manitoba government has countered by arguing that the exclusion cannot be reviewed by a court because it was a funding decision. Justice Neville noted that the government's previous filings provided no information regarding who made the decisions, how they were made, or why they were made. The judge characterized the government's stance as displaying “a baffling coyness” regarding the process.

cards.headline: Central-north Amazonia experiencing alarming temperature and dryness increases, study finds

pages.text: Research published in September in the journal Nature identifies the central-north part of the Amazon Basin as the vanguard of an “alarming” increase in temperatures and dry conditions. While southern Amazonia has long been recognized as a climate change hotspot due to deforestation and forest fires, this new study indicates a shift in the region's warming patterns. By analyzing satellite, aircraft, and observation station data from 1981 to 2023, researchers found that extreme temperatures across all of Amazonia increased more than twice as quickly as annual mean temperatures.

During a forest census near Manaus, northern Brazil, in October 2023, biologist Aretha Guimarães and her colleagues from Brazil’s National Institute of Amazonian Research (INPA) observed significant environmental distress as fire season began. Guimarães reported that the team encountered smoke so thick it obscured vision and heat so intense that conventional masks were unusable, forcing researchers to use wet bandages to breathe. Guimarães told Mongabay that the team witnessed unprecedented animal mortality, specifically noting that dead sloths were found in every part of the forest they studied, including some still hanging from branches. The researchers assumed most of the sloths could not move quickly enough to find water as temperatures rose.

cards.headline: Gitxsan hereditary chiefs call for halt to rail cargo following diesel leak from Skeena River derailment

pages.text: The Gitxsan Huwilp Government is calling for an immediate stop to train hauling near its traditional territory after a Canadian National Railway train derailed into the Skeena River in British Columbia. The Gitxsan hereditary chiefs' demand follows a second landslide and derailment in the area within eight months. Simogyet Skogam'Lahkx Toby Howard stated the incident shows derailments remain a clear and present danger to the food security of the Gitxsan people, noting that fish in the Skeena feed eagles, seals, and the Gitxsan people. Howard said train hauling is dangerous and must stop immediately because people were transported to hospital and another train is in the river.

On November 17, 2026, a rockslide caused a Canadian National Railway train carrying forestry products to go off the tracks approximately 17 kilometres west of Terrace, B.C. The derailment involved two locomotives and five railcars carrying multiple containers of forest products. Images from the scene showed several cars off the track and multiple containers in the water. CN Rail reported that diesel leaked from a locomotive and stated that crews are working to contain the spill and repair the route. Two CN Rail employees were taken to hospital following the incident but have since been released.

This is the second spill recorded in the area in less than a year. In March, a mudslide derailed grain cars along the Skeena during extreme weather, resulting in 7,949 litres of diesel being released, of which 3,421 litres were unaccounted for, according to the B.C. government's spill response page. Prior to the March incident, there were no major spill reports along the rail line from Terrace to Prince Rupert over the past decade.

cards.headline: Astronomers discover unusual triple-star system 28 light-years from Earth

pages.text: An international team of scientists has discovered Welopōʻai, a triple-star system located just 28 light-years from Earth that challenges current understanding of how stars evolve and interact. The system consists of a red dwarf—a star much dimmer than the sun—and two white dwarfs, which are the extremely dense remnants of sunlike stars that have exhausted their fuel. The discovery was made by a team led by the Trottier Institute for Research on Exoplanets (IREx) at Université de Montréal and was detailed in a study published in Astronomy & Astrophysics.

Researchers stumbled upon the configuration while searching for planets orbiting the red dwarf using the SPectropolarimètre InfraROUge (SPIRou) instrument at the Canada-France-Hawaii Telescope on Maunakea, Hawaii. SPIRou is designed to detect exoplanets by measuring tiny changes in a star's velocity caused by the gravitational pull of orbiting planets. However, the red dwarf in this system exhibited velocity variations of nearly 16 kilometers per second (10 miles per second), which was more than 1,000 times larger than expected for a planet. Following several years of follow-up observations, the team established that the unseen companion had a mass greater than half that of the sun.
